youtube.title: DR CLARE CRAIG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with UK consultant pathologist Dr Clare Craig, co-chair of HART (Health ethics Advocacy & Research Team), about how “the greatest good for the greatest number” results in the justification for sacrificing individuals—especially when decisions are made at population level rather than with informed consent between doctor and patient. She says its time to bring medical ethics back. Discover more from HART on Substack and Clare Craig on Substack Follow Dr Clare Craig on X and HART on Facebook and X For Clare's book: Spiked: A shot in the dark

youtube.title: JAN RIVERS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Jan Rivers, spokesperson for Genspect NZ, about the American Society of Plastic Surgeons recommending delaying gender-related surgeries until at least 19, citing weak evidence and potential long-term harm. Rivers links the shift to rising US legal and consumer-protection scrutiny, arguing surgeons are “end of the chain” and exposed to downstream harms. The discussion turns to New Zealand’s largely affirmative-only counselling settings, the puberty-blockers judicial review due in May, and concern that advocacy groups are shaping medical policy. For more information visit Genspect NZ or Public Good or follow Genspect on X

youtube.title: PAUL’S MAILBAG
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan dips into a packed RCR mailbag, reflecting listener reactions to interviews spanning health leadership, gene technology, COVID accountability, protest policing, climate narratives and global governance. Feedback features robust debate around Winston Peters and the Gene Tech Bill, deep scepticism of pandemic responses, and calls for greater scrutiny of power and institutions.

youtube.title: RAMESH THAKUR
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Professor Ramesh Thakur, former UN Assistant Secretary-General and leading scholar of international security, at a moment of deep global disruption. They unpack Australia’s hastily introduced speech laws and the wider trend of law-fare in Western democracies. The conversation also covers the Monroe Doctrine and Donald Trump’s National Security Strategy and erosion of international law with unilateral power moves in Venezuela, Iran and Greenland and what his Board of Peace signals for the future of global governance.

youtube.title: MATT SHELTON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Dr Matt Shelton from New Zealand Doctors Speaking Out with Science (NZDSOS) about a new trio of preprint studies investigating “rubbery white clots” reported by embalmers. Shelton says literature reviews found no prior record, and describes the clots as tough, fibrous structures lacking red cells, platelets and plasminogen, suggesting they form in life and may resist breakdown. He references New Zealand embalmer Brenton Faithful, US survey work by Tom Haviland, and calls for independent scrutiny and journal publication. Discover more from NZDSOS or follow them on Facebook and X

youtube.title: LUCY ROGERS
youtube.summary: Simon O’Connor speaks with Lucy Rogers, a junior criminal defence lawyer who was unlawfully arrested during a November 2023 protest and released without charge. An IPCA investigation later found the arrest unjustified, and she is now pursuing legal action for wrongful arrest and Bill of Rights breaches. Lucy has been involved in counter protesting anti-Israel protests regularly for two years. For further information: Lucy Rogers Kiwi Blog Post Toitu Te Aroha protest footage Simon O'Connor: On Point Substack NZ Against Hamas Facebook group

youtube.title: RODNEY’S REFLECTION
youtube.summary: Rodney reflects on Chloe Swarbrick’s political views, questioning her positions on capitalism, colonialism, and the parliamentary system. He challenges her to clarify the alternatives she proposes, suggesting they may resemble totalitarianism or tribalism. He also encourages her to examine countries with similar systems and questions her connections with Hamas.
